title: Course Unique By ID
prompt: A course import may contain duplicate ids. Write a function that keeps only the first record for each id while preserving original order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: courseUniqueById([{"id":"1","label":"A"},{"id":"1","label":"B"},{"id":"2","label":"C"}]) produces [{"id":"1","label":"A"},{"id":"2","label":"C"}]. Track the key that defines equality and retain one representative according to the contract’s ordering rule.

Compare “handles no duplicates”: input [[{"id":"1","label":"A"}]] produces [{"id":"1","label":"A"}]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Track the key that defines equality and retain one representative according to the contract’s ordering rule.

Tempting mistake: Deduplicating objects by reference does not deduplicate equal IDs. Keep duplicate handling and output order explicit.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles no duplicates”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
